Topological effective sample size across RevBayes runs

Source: R/trees.R
TreeESS.Rd

Estimates the effective sample size of tree topology across one or more independent RevBayes runs, using the lower of the Frechet correlation and median pseudo-ESS statistics (the pair used throughout Smith 2026), as recommended by Fabreti & Hohna (2022) and Magee et al. (2024).

Usage

TreeESS(runFiles, burnin = 0.25, cap = 1000, threshold = 200)

Arguments

runFiles

Character vector of paths to RevBayes .trees files, one per independent run.

burnin

Proportion of samples discarded from each trace.

cap

Maximum number of trees retained per run (traces longer than this are evenly thinned before the ESS calculation, which scales poorly with sample size).

threshold

Minimum summed ESS (across runs) for convergence.

Value

A list with elements ok (logical, whether threshold is met), perRun (a data frame of per-run ESS estimates), summed (the two ESS statistics summed across runs) and minEss (the smaller of the two).
